info.name: QA Learning — JSONPlaceholder
info.description:
P1 — the same public API the Robot suites in tests/api/ already cover, done again in Postman.

The practice is not new; the tool is. What is worth noticing is where the two differ:

- Robot puts assertions in the suite, in a language built for them. Postman puts them in a JavaScript `Tests` tab, so an assertion is code and can drift into logic.
- Robot resolves variables from a variable file or the command line. Postman has four scopes (collection, environment, local, global) and the narrowest one wins.
- Robot chains requests by returning a value into a variable. Postman writes into `pm.collectionVariables`, which persists for the whole run.

Run it in the app, or headless:
  newman run postman/qa-learning.postman_collection.json -e postman/environments/public.postman_environment.json

exec: // A collection-level test runs after EVERY request in the collection.
// This is the Postman idea with no Robot equivalent: two checks written
// once and applied to everything, including requests added later.

variable.description: Filled in by 'Create a post' and read by the request after it. Collection scope, so it survives across requests in one run.

item.description: GETs only. Nothing here changes anything, so the order does not matter — the Day 18 rule, in another tool.

// type passes every existence check. Assert the type, not the key.

exec: // The negative case. A suite that only ever asks for things that exist
// has not tested the lookup, it has tested the happy path.

item.name: Write
item.description: The requests that hand something to the API, and the one that checks what happened next.

exec: // Pre-request script: runs BEFORE the request is sent, which is where
// test data gets built. Same job as Random Email in DataHelpers.py -
// a fixed title passes once and then collides with itself.
pm.test('It echoes back exactly what was sent', function () {
pm.test('It hands back an id', function () {
// Chaining: this is how a value reaches the next request. Collection
// scope rather than environment scope, so a run does not quietly edit
// the environment file that other runs share.

item.name: The created post was never stored

exec: // A 201 is a claim, not a receipt - Robot Day 22, reached from the other
// direction. JSONPlaceholder is a fake API: it answers 201 with a
// convincing id and stores nothing, so asking for that id gives 404.
// This test asserts the behaviour that is actually there rather than the
// one that ought to be. Against a real service it would be the opposite,
// and it is worth knowing which of the two you are looking at.
pm.test('The id that came back cannot be fetched', function () {
